draft.title: Mass spectrometry
card: In a mass spectrometer, molecules are hit with high-energy electrons. This knocks an electron off each molecule and makes a positive ion, called the molecular ion.

The molecular ion often breaks into smaller fragments. Only fragments that are positive ions reach the detector. The spectrum plots the mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) against abundance. Most ions carry a charge of +1, so m/z is the ion's mass.
The peak with the highest m/z is usually the molecular ion. Its m/z value equals the molar mass of the molecule, in g/mol.
The gaps between peaks show which pieces were lost. A loss of 15 fits a CH3 group, and a loss of 29 fits a C2H5 group. The pattern of fragments gives clues to the structure.
draft.remember: The molecular ion peak gives the molar mass. The fragment peaks give clues to the structure.

a.q: A compound has a mass spectrum with its highest m/z peak at 72. What does this peak most likely show?
opts: The molar mass of the compound is 72 g/mol
The compound has a CH3 group of mass 72
a.why: The peak with the highest m/z is usually the molecular ion, and its m/z equals the molar mass. It does not count atoms. A CH3 group has a mass of 15, so a loss of 15 would show a CH3 group, not a peak at 72.
a.clue: The molecular ion has lost only one electron, so its mass is the mass of the whole molecule.

b.q: A compound has a molecular ion peak at m/z 58 and a strong fragment peak at m/z 43. What does the fragment peak suggest?
opts: The molecule lost a CH3 group of mass 15
The molecule lost a C2H5 group of mass 29
The compound has a molar mass of 43 g/mol
The molecule lost a hydrogen atom of mass 1
b.why: 58 minus 43 is 15, which matches a lost CH3 group. A loss of 29 would leave a fragment at 29, not 43. The molar mass is given by the molecular ion at 58, not by a fragment peak.
b.clue: Subtract the fragment m/z from the molecular ion m/z, then match the difference to a group.

a.best: The molar mass of the compound is 72 g/mol

b.best: The molecule lost a CH3 group of mass 15
